inputs.text: The Liberal Party is fracturing from within as MPs including Andrew Hastie push for higher taxes on gas companies and an end to concessions for property investors. These proposals mark an essential step toward confronting structural inequality by compelling powerful corporations and wealthy property owners to contribute fairly rather than relying on built-in advantages that continue widening gaps for workers and vulnerable communities. Angus Taylor's outright rejection of the ideas exposes the party's deep resistance to reforms that would challenge corporate power or historical privileges, blocking any real progress on labor rights and economic justice. The leader's refusal to echo attacks on Donald Trump and evasion on backing the US and Israel against Iran fit the same pattern of clinging to outdated alliances that divert attention from the urgent domestic institutional changes needed to protect marginalized groups.
